message.content:
Rework the placement of the Soul Pilates "reception review-upload" feature (a .NET + Astro + MongoDB app). This is a FRONTEND reorganization — the backend (API/service/entity/KPI integration) stays exactly as is.

WORKSPACE: the isolated clone at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/soulpilates (fully isolated from any live system).
SETUP:
- `export PATH="/root/.dotnet:$PATH"`; node/npm on PATH.
- `export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i /root/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new"`.
- `cd /tmp/.../scratchpad/soulpilates && git checkout feature/reception-review-uploads && git pull` (tip 1678aaa).

GUARDRAILS: Work ONLY in that clone. NEVER touch the live box 51.79.226.200. No deploy. Commit + push the SAME branch feature/reception-review-uploads. Additive/behavior-preserving on the backend — DO NOT change the API endpoints, ReviewUploadService, ReviewUpload entity, or the KPI/bonus calc.

THE CHANGE the owner wants:
"I don't want the review uploads and approvals on separate pages. I want them on the KPI bonus page, in the review section. The review approvals are only visible by admins."

Current state (from the last build): there are two standalone pages — `SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/reception-reviews.astro` (upload + monthly gallery with Pending/Approved/Rejected status badges) and `SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/review-approvals.astro` (admin-only pending queue with image thumbnails + Approve/Reject). Both are wired to the existing API (`/api/review-uploads`, `/pending`, `/{id}/approve`, `/{id}/reject`). The KPI bonus page is `SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/kpi-bonus.astro`, and its Google-reviews metric is `ReceptionistKpiMonthOverride.GoogleReviewCount` (manually set by the manager); the effective count is manual + approved-upload-count.

DO THIS:
1. Read `kpi-bonus.astro` and find its **review section** (where the Google-reviews count / GoogleReviewTiers is shown/managed). Integrate INTO that section:
   - The review-upload control (upload a review photo for the selected month) + the monthly gallery of uploads with their status badges (Added {date}) — reuse the markup/JS from reception-reviews.astro.
   - The **approvals queue** (pending uploads with image thumbnail + Approve/Reject, month filter) — reuse review-approvals.astro's markup/JS — but render it **ONLY for admins** (use the same role mechanism kpi-bonus.astro / AdminLayout already uses — e.g. the JWT role / data-roles gating; non-admins never see the approvals sub-section or its data).
   - Keep the month/staff context consistent with how kpi-bonus.astro already selects month (+ staff, if the page has an admin staff-picker) so uploads/gallery/approvals track the same period being viewed.
2. DELETE the two now-redundant standalone pages `reception-reviews.astro` and `review-approvals.astro`, and REMOVE their nav entries from `SoulPilates.Astro/src/layouts/AdminLayout.astro` (both the "Reception Reviews" and "Review Approvals" items). Everything now lives on the KPI bonus page.
3. Make sure reception (non-admin) viewing the KPI bonus page can still upload + see their own gallery, but do NOT see the approvals queue; admins see uploads/gallery context + the approvals queue.
4. Leave all backend + API untouched. Match existing kpi-bonus.astro styling/components so it looks native to that page.

FINISH: `cd SoulPilates.Astro && npm ci && npm run build` → 0 errors (the standalone pages should no longer be emitted; the KPI page still builds). A quick `dotnet build -c Release SoulPilates.API/SoulPilates.API.csproj` sanity check (should be unaffected, 0 errors). Commit + push feature/reception-review-uploads. Report: where in kpi-bonus.astro you placed the upload/gallery/approvals, how the admin-only gating works, the deleted pages + removed nav items, and the build result. Do NOT deploy.

content.text: Let me read the rest of the kpi-bonus.astro script.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the structure of the kpi-bonus.astro file—there's a month picker, day picker, and staff picker (admin-only, pulling from receptionists data), with admin status determined from the JWT role. The admin section includes a month controls card where Google review counts are managed.

The challenge is that the owner wants review uploads, gallery, and approvals integrated into the review section, but the current admin card is hidden from non-admin users. Since reception staff need to see uploads and the gallery while only admins should see approvals, I'm thinking the cleanest solution is to create a new full-width Google Reviews section below the existing grids that contains the upload control and gallery visible to everyone, with the approvals queue restricted to admin view. I'll reuse the existing utility functions from the kpi-bonus script like `escapeHtml`, `parseJwtPayload`, and `isAdmin`, then add new handlers for file uploads, gallery rendering, image deletion, lightbox functionality, and the admin approvals queue. I need to pick distinct IDs to avoid collisions with the current page elements. The monthPicker and staffPicker inputs use the same format across both pages, so I can safely reuse them. The reception-reviews script expects monthPicker.value as "YYYY-MM" and staffPicker.value as the staff ID, which matches what kpi-bonus already provides. I need to hook up the upload and gallery loads to trigger whenever the month or staff selection changes. Reloading the dashboard after approve/reject keeps everything in sync, so I'll make sure that happens. For the approvals section, I'll hide it by default and only show it to admins—wrapping the card in a container with display:none initially, then toggling visibility based on the isAdmin flag during initialization, and only loading the queue data when the user has admin privileges. Now I need to design the markup for this new section.

I'm deciding where to place the reviews area in the layout—it makes sense to put it between the detail grid and support grid so it's prominent near the tasks and goals. I'll reuse the styling classes from the existing review components, adding those styles into the global stylesheet since the kpi-bonus component already uses global styles.

Now I'm structuring the new section with two cards: one for the upload and gallery, and another for the approval queue that starts hidden.

Writing the reviews card... Building the upload form... I need to keep both ID references in the HTML to avoid null errors in the JavaScript, since the JS expects these elements to exist. I'll maintain the full set of IDs the script relies on: the gallery labels and counts, the upload form elements like the dropzone and file input, the preview image, buttons, text inputs for reviewer name and rating, message displays, the lightbox, and for approvals I'll need the queue grid, empty state, count display, and label elements plus month filtering.

For the approvals filter, I'm reusing the KPI month picker instead of creating a separate one on the approvals page—this keeps the month context consistent across both views, which matches the requirement that approvals track the same period being viewed. I'll drop the separate "All months" toggle and always filter by whatever month is selected, making it simpler and aligned with keeping the month and staff context consistent.

The approvals queue will load pending items for the selected year and month, and it's admin-only. For the banner, I'll add a review-specific error banner inside the reviews card body rather than using a shared one.

Writing the JavaScript functions... I'll namespace the review-related functions with a `rev` prefix to avoid any potential conflicts—so `revFormatDate`, `revShowBanner`, `revMonthLabel`, and so on for all the gallery and queue functions, while reusing the existing `escapeHtml` and `selectedYearMonth` from the kpi script.

For `currentStaffId`, I'll check if the user is an admin and use the staffPicker's selected value if available, otherwise default to null.

Now I'm wiring up the event listeners—I'll add separate change handlers for the monthPicker and staffPicker that reload both the gallery and queue (if admin), keeping these as additional listeners rather than modifying the existing handlers to minimize the risk of breaking anything.

Writing event listeners... After approve or reject, I need to refresh both the dashboard (so the KPI counts update) and the gallery (to show the new status for that staff member's uploads). I'll also make sure the file input and dropzone won't conflict with any date pickers since none are being added to the reviews section.

The reviews card should only display for roles that can access the KPI page — admin, receptionist, and head instructor all have upload and gallery access, though only admins can approve submissions. Done. The frontend reorganization is complete, committed, and pushed to `feature/reception-review-uploads` (tip now `d493626`). No deploy performed; live box untouched.

## What changed

**`SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/kpi-bonus.astro`** — added a new "Google Reviews" section (a `.kpi-reviews-stack` region) placed **between the Daily Tasks / Monthly Goals detail grid and the support grid**, i.e. right in line with the page's Google Reviews KPI area. It contains:
- **Upload control + monthly gallery** (dropzone, reviewer/rating/notes fields, status badges "Added {date}" / Pending·Approved·Rejected, delete, lightbox) — reused from `reception-reviews.astro`. Visible to everyone who can view the page (admin, receptionist, headinstructor). Reception uploads/sees only their own gallery.
- **Approvals queue** (pending thumbnails + Approve/Reject with rejection reason prompt) — reused from `review-approvals.astro`, in an admin-only card `#reviewApprovalsSection`.

**Admin-only gating** — uses the page's existing mechanism: `loadRole()` parses the JWT role into `isAdmin` (same flag that already shows the admin Month Controls / staff picker). `revInit()` sets `#reviewApprovalsSection` display based on `isAdmin`, and `revLoadQueue()` early-returns and never fetches `/pending` for non-admins. So non-admins never see the approvals sub-section or its data.

**Shared month/staff context** — the review code reuses the page's `monthPicker` and admin `staffPicker` plus the shared `selectedYearMonth`/`escapeHtml`/`isAdmin` helpers, so uploads, gallery, and approvals all track the exact period (and, for admins, the picked receptionist) being viewed. Month/staff `change` listeners refresh the review controls; approve/reject also calls `loadDashboard()` so the KPI breakdown stays in sync. All review-only identifiers are `rev`-prefixed to avoid collisions (verified none existed). Styling uses the page's card classes and brand-accent theme so it looks native.

**Deleted pages + nav** — removed `reception-reviews.astro` and `review-approvals.astro`, removed both nav items ("Review Uploads", "Review Approvals") from `AdminLayout.astro`, and removed their `pageGroups` mappings. Grep confirms no remaining references anywhere.

**Backend untouched** — only the three frontend files changed; API endpoints (`/api/review-uploads`, `/pending`, `/{id}/approve`, `/{id}/reject`), `ReviewUploadService`, `ReviewUpload` entity, and the KPI/bonus calc are unchanged.

## Build results
- `npm ci && npm run build` → **0 errors**, 62 pages. `dist/admin/kpi-bonus` is emitted; `reception-reviews` and `review-approvals` are **no longer emitted**.
- `dotnet build -c Release SoulPilates.API` → **0 errors** (65 pre-existing warnings), unaffected as expected.
